source.title: Microsoft Outlook v1 Add attachment reads the binary field name from item 0 for every item

labels.name: status:in-linear
labels.description: Issue or PR is now in Linear

source.body:
### Bug Description

In packages/nodes-base/nodes/Microsoft/Outlook/v1/MicrosoftOutlookV1.node.ts, resource Message Attachment, operation Add, the per-item loop reads the binary property name with item index 0: this.getNodeParameter('binaryPropertyName', 0). The binary data checks right after it use items[i].

If the field name is an expression that differs per item, every item uses the field name of the first item. messageId and additionalFields in the same loop already use the current index i.

This is the same kind of bug as #44021, but not a duplicate. That issue covers the v2 operation (v2/actions/messageAttachment/add.operation.ts). This one covers the v1 node file, which is not fixed by the v2 PR.

### To Reproduce

1. Use Microsoft Outlook node version 1 (existing workflow). Resource: Message Attachment. Operation: Add.
2. Two input items. Item 1 has binary data on the field "data". Item 2 has binary data on the field "attachment". Each item has a "field" value in its JSON that names its binary field.
3. Set "Binary Property" to {{ $json.field }}.
4. Run the node.
5. Item 2 looks up "data" instead of "attachment" and fails.

### Expected behavior

The binary field name is read with the current item index. Item 2 uses "attachment".

### Debug Info

Found by reading the source on master. Verified with a unit test that uses two items with different binary field names. The test fails without the fix. A fix PR will follow.

### Operating System

macOS

### n8n Version

2.48.0

### Node.js Version

24.20.0

### Database

SQLite (default)

### Execution mode

main (default)

### Hosting

self hosted

comments.author: goutham-valugula
comments.text: Confirmed in current `MicrosoftOutlookV1.node.ts`: the Add operation loop is at lines 654–658, and it calls `this.getNodeParameter("binaryPropertyName", 0)` while `messageId` and `additionalFields` use `i`. The later binary lookup uses `items[i]`, so an item-specific expression can select one name for every item. Passing `i` to `getNodeParameter` matches the surrounding loop and the v1 download operation’s per-item lookup. The issue’s two-item case is a focused regression test for this.

comments.author: grinem
comments.text: Spot on, thanks for tracking down that parity gap with #44021. Swapping `0` for `i` in `this.getNodeParameter('binaryPropertyName', i)` is definitely the right fix.

comments.author: goutham-valugula
comments.text: I verified the mismatch in the current source: the Message Attachment Add loop reads `messageId` and `additionalFields` with index `i`, but reads `binaryPropertyName` with index `0` before looking up binary data on `items[i]`. That makes the reported per-item expression case consistent with the implementation; using `i` for that parameter also matches the download operation immediately below.
